newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes firm with Brent seen moving west.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes firm with Brent seen moving west.

text.p: LONDON, Dec 10 (Reuter) North Sea physical crude markets firmed on Tuesday, underpinned by a stronger Dated Brent trade, although the Brent paper market eased lower.
A wet Brent cargo loading Dec 21-23 traded at Jan Brent +33 cents, the buyer the Wall Street trader that already holds some five Brent cargoes, traders said.
Dated Brent last traded on Monday at just Jan Brent +22.5 cents for a Dec 20-22 loader.
Traders said that Dated Brent's rebound looked fairly secure given an open transatlantic arbitrage. "The U.S. is tight and there's certainly a potential to sell cargoes," said one trader.
The buyer of today's Brent cargo was believed to be working at least one VLCC to the U.S.
Differentials for other North Sea grades were talked steady, with few cargoes left unsold for December.
An Oseberg cargo loading end-Dec was bought by a German refiner for Jan 1-5 delivery on an out-turn basis, the price equivalent to Dated Brent +47/48.
Statfjord was sold out for December, while three Osebergs, one Ekofisk and one Draugen remained, a Norwegian producer said.
Jan Brent paper was trading some 55 cents down at $23.55 a barrel at 1830 GMT in line with the IPE screen.
Jan paper traded earlier at $23.88 and $23.92 a barrel.
Intermonth spreads eased from Monday with Jan/Feb talked around +55/+58 and Feb/March at +60/+63, having traded at +62 cents.
Two Brent cfds for next week traded at Jan Brent -5 cents, after a Dec 23-27 cfd changed hands at Feb Brent +40 cents.
In the Mediterranean, two Urals cargoes, loading Dec 10-15, were traded on Monday on a private and confidential basis, with the discount to Dated Brent pegged around 15/20 cents.
